- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) after price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5–7 forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often fails to capture mean reversion; reduce forecast slope in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment up but price down), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction.
- In low-volatility periods (sentiment flat or near 0), model often overfits recent history; apply smoothing or reduce forecast amplitude.
- Model underperforms when sentiment is mixed or volatile (±0.3–0.6); use sentiment-weighted average to dampen overconfidence in single trend.
